_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS R1247's LAW IS NOT VACUOUS — run it from the
WHAT THE LAW IS. `AtomicStore::load` works out the generation the file
declares before anything can fail on shape, runs the forward-migration arms
keyed off it, and — until R1247 — dropped it on every failure path. So the
two unattended-loop kits, whose stores are generation 23, answered `query`
and `validate-workspace` with the name of one removed shape and no distance
at all. One shape name reads like one repair.
SO THE FOUR INJECTIONS ARE THE FOUR WAYS THE DISTANCE STOPS BEING TOLD, and
every one of them is silent in the direction that reads as a working build:
the wrap never happens, the clause loses its numbers, the wrapper eats the
cause a caller matches on, and a generation is invented for bytes that never
yielded one. None of them fails to compile and none prints an error.
RUN IT LOCALLY. The harness edits this tree and writes the firing record
beside this file, so a run sent to a build machine leaves its evidence on a
throwaway copy (R1205's carry, and the `writes` line in the declaration).

injections.name: the-wrap-never-happens
injections.why: the whole repair, reverted by one character. A store that is behind leaves with its shape error exactly as it did before R1247, which is the state the two kits were measured in: true, actionable about one shape, and silent about the twenty-three generations behind it

injections.name: the-clause-loses-its-numbers
injections.why: the wrapper still wraps, so every match arm and every caller behaves, and the only thing missing is the sentence a person reads. A refusal that carries the distance in a field nothing prints is the same as one that never carried it. R1254 RE-AIMED THIS ANCHOR without changing what it claims: the attribute now also prints what stands between the two generations, and the harness refused the old text as `occurs 0 times` rather than letting a proof nobody runs sit here looking like one that holds

injections.name: the-wrapper-eats-the-cause
injections.why: the cost of wrapping, if the way back out is wrong. Callers that match the taxonomy rather than the sentence — the migration work-list is one — get the wrapper handed back instead of the refusal under it, and a match arm that no longer fires reads as a store that no longer has that problem. Three tests name it because the R708 and R873 work-list laws were BOTH written against a store that is behind, so they read the cause through this accessor: that they go red here is the accessor being load-bearing, not a stray

injections.name: a-generation-is-invented-for-bytes-that-never-gave-one
injections.why: the other half of the law, and the direction a later refactor is likeliest to break: wrapping the raw parse too would put a generation on a file whose bytes are not JSON, which is a number nobody read off anything. The clause would then be decoration rather than a reading
